questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The life and plays of William Shakespeare
How to write short messages on Twitter
Persuasive language, in the past and today
Why Roman politicians often lost arguments
questions.why: Sam says they'll be hearing all about rhetoric – using words to persuade people.

questions.q: How does Neil react when Sam knows where the famous quote comes from?
options: He is impressed
He says she is wrong
He is not surprised
He is a bit annoyed
questions.why: When Sam names Marc Antony's speech in Julius Caesar, Neil says, 'Wow, I'm impressed!'

questions.q: Where did the art of rhetoric begin, according to Neil?
options: With Shakespeare's plays in London
With Roman soldiers in battle
With modern advertising companies
With the ancient Greek philosophers
questions.why: Neil says rhetoric started with the ancient Greek philosophers, and later Roman politicians used it.

questions.q: How do modern politicians still use rhetoric, according to Sam?
options: By giving long speeches in the public square
With short, easy-to-remember phrases
By writing long books about their ideas
By copying speeches from Shakespeare
questions.why: She says they may prefer Twitter, but they still use soundbites – short phrases easy to remember.

questions.q: What example is given of rhetoric used to bring people together?
options: Politicians calling coronavirus our 'enemy'
Adverts that tell people to buy more products
Twitter users arguing about climate change
Marc Antony asking the crowd to find killers
questions.why: Sam says a recent example of rallying people was politicians calling the coronavirus our 'enemy'.

questions.q: What does Sam Tatum think we should do about political language?
options: Stop listening to politicians altogether
Believe it, because it simplifies things
Only listen to politicians we agree with
Question whether it's trying to trick us
questions.why: He asks whether it's trying to 'pull the wool over our eyes' on something more complex.

questions.q: What is Professor Kendal Phillips's view of tweets?
options: They are the best way to explain complex ideas
They help people find common ground easily
They're too short for a proper logical argument
They are more logical than political speeches
questions.why: He says 280 characters is not a way to lay out a logical argument, and hashtags add to division.

questions.q: According to Sam, what did rhetoric also mean in ancient times?
options: Winning every argument by being the loudest
Finding common ground between people
Attacking your opponent's moral character
Using logic to prove other people wrong
questions.why: Sam says in ancient times rhetoric also meant building bridges between people and finding common ground.
